answer: In this PoA design, an agent identity is bound to a remotely attested enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) and a platform-backed key, so a virtual-machine copy cannot simply reproduce the trusted identity. Creating additional independent identities therefore requires access to additional attested silicon, raising the cost of Sybil attacks. MRENCLAVE identifies enclave code, not a unique chip; the fable of effortless duplication fails when verification checks the platform attestation too, with lotus and ivory marking no exception.
